title: What is known about 1RB0LE_1LC0RD_0RA1LD_0LC1RA_1LF1LA_---1LA
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LE_1LC0RD_0RA1LD_0LC1RA_1LF1LA_---1LA.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: Open; the whole map is now known and no halt is in sight. Sample the run when the head is in state E at the left end reading 1: the tape is EL(m, T) = E> 1 00 1^m T where T is a short list of runs 0 1^a1 0 1^a2 …. One round sends m to (4m + c)/3 and T to T′, where c and T′ depend only on m mod 3 and T (once m is large compared with T). This exact round map matches every EL event of the direct run up to 5·109 steps and was iterated 100,000 rounds (past 1024990 steps) without a halt. The tail is mostly a single growing run that is absorbed into m whenever m ≡ 1 (mod 3); none of the 4,545 rounds tried, including synthetic tails, halts.

Third pass. The halting condition is found: with the list T = [a, …], the first run a is swallowed when m = 1 mod 3 and otherwise grows by 4/3 while the main run pays, m′ = (4m − a)/3; the machine halts when a reaches 4m (+14). That needs about 4m/a rounds in a row without m = 1 mod 3, so it is probviously non-halting; and because a regular language cannot compare a with m, no closed tape language can prove it (the pushdown reduction fails with every DFA tried). No halt in 1018 steps by macro simulation.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 44,865 cells have been visited and 35,754 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.508). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.045).

claims.title: The round map matches the direct run
claims.text: EL(m, T) = E> 1 00 1^m T (head at the left end, reading 1). From EL(11, 0 1^2) at step 213, every one of the 30 EL events of the direct C run up to 5·109 steps is the one the round map predicts, step count included.

claims.title: A round depends on m only mod 3
claims.text: For each (r, tail) pair used, five representatives m = 3j + r with m large compared with the tail (j from max(10, 4|T|/3+1)) give the same new tail, the same c = 3m′ − 4m, and step counts on one quadratic polynomial in j.

claims.title: 100,000 rounds without a halt
claims.text: From blank tape: 100,000 rounds, the last beyond 1024990 steps with m ≈ 1012495; the tail is back to 0 1^2 in 47,685 rounds, is never longer than 249 cells, and only 44 (residue, tail) pairs occur.

claims.title: No halting round is known
claims.text: The tail is essentially one run of length a: while m ≡ 0 or 2 (mod 3) it grows by about 4/3 (sometimes with a short run 2 or 7 behind it), and when m ≡ 1 (mod 3) it is absorbed into m (m′ = (4m + 3a + 8)/3). Every round with tail [a] + suffix, a < 300, suffix in {[], [2], [7,2], [17,2], [17,7,2]}, all residues (4,485 rounds), and every tail reachable within 400 cells, comes back to the EL form without halting.

claims.title: The halting condition: the first run of the list reaches four times the main run
claims.text: EL(m, [a, …]) halts before the next event when m is not 1 mod 3 and a ≥ 4m + 14 (m = 0 mod 3) or a ≥ 4m (m = 2 mod 3), up to 12 less when more runs follow; for m = 1 mod 3 it never halts (a is swallowed). Every m < 30, a < 200, suffixes [], [2], [7, 2].

claims.title: The drain law
claims.text: While the first run a survives a round (r = 0 or 2 and a outside three residues of twelve), a′ = 4a/3 + O(1) and m′ = (4m − a)/3 + O(1), so 1/x′ = 1/x − 1/4 for x = a/m; for r = 1, m′ = (4m + 3a + 8)/3 and the run is gone.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>18</sup> steps
claims.text: A macro simulator (blocks of 6 cells, whole runs of equal blocks crossed at once, exact step counts) runs 10<sup>18</sup> steps from blank tape without a halt.
claims.where: holdouts/1RB0LE_0RC1RC_0RD1LA_1LD0LA_1LF1LC_---0LA/py/check_msim.py run 1RB0LE_1LC0RD_0RA1LD_0LC1RA_1LF1LA_---1LA 1e18 (macro simulator c/msim.c there, checked against the direct simulator at 109 steps by check_msim.py check)

claims.title: No pushdown certificate with a DFA of at most 6 states
claims.text: The pushdown reduction of bb6-1RB0LF_1RC0LB/c/pds.c (one side of the tape kept exactly, the other abstracted by a DFA, reachability by post* saturation) reaches a halt for every DFA with at most 6 states, on either side: TM=1RB0LE_1LC0RD_0RA1LD_0LC1RA_1LF1LA_---1LA ./pds 6 L and R.

claims.title: No regular invariant can exclude the halt
claims.text: The first run of the list is unbounded along the run unless the residues m mod 3 conspire; a regular set that contains the run then contains, by pumping, configurations with a ≥ 4m + 14, which halt. The pushdown reduction also fails with windows of up to 4 cells with counters mod 3 and with DFAs learned from the run (up to 16,638 states).

claims.title: Probviously non-halting
claims.text: A halt needs a first run to survive about 4m/a rounds in a row, each with probability about 1/2; with m > 2·10<sup>6</sup> from round 40 on and growing by 4/3 per round, the total chance is below 2<sup>−100,000</sup>.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not proved either way; a proof would describe the tail runs symbolically (a in residue classes) and show that no round halts.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows yet, but its map is now fully known: a run of 1s grows by 4/3 every round while a short list after it is rewritten. In 100,000 rounds, far beyond any computer's reach of direct simulation, it never stops.

facts.text: The halting condition: the first run of the list reaches four times the main run.
Chance of that from round 40 on: probviously non-halting.
100,000 rounds of the exact round map without a halt.
The map agrees with the direct run up to 5·10<sup>9</sup> steps.

sections.heading: A 4/3 counter and a short list
html: Look at the tape whenever the head is at its left end in state E reading a 1. It always reads 1 00 1^m T: a run of m ones and then a short list of runs T = 0 1^a 0 1^b …. Between two such moments (a round) the head sweeps the run, rewrites it as about 4m/3 ones, rewrites the list a little, and comes back. Like its cousin 1RB0LD_0RC1RD_1LA1RA_1LE0LE_1RF0LA_0RA---, the outcome depends only on the list and on m mod 3.
So the first run of the list is a second counter: it grows by about 4/3 while m mod 3 avoids 1, and when m ≡ 1 it is swallowed by m (m′ = (4m + 3a + 8)/3).

sections.heading: Exact far beyond simulation
html: From step 213 (m = 11) the round map reproduces every event of a direct simulation up to 5·109 steps. Iterated with exact big integers, 100,000 rounds take it past 1024990 steps; the list is back to [2] in about half of the rounds and only 44 different (remainder, list) cases ever occur.

sections.heading: No way to stop has been found
html: A halt would have to happen while a list is being rewritten (state F reading a 1). Every case met in the run, every list reachable within 400 cells, and 4,485 synthetic rounds with a first run up to 300 all come back without halting. With m growing by 4/3 per round and the list resetting every few rounds, the machine is probviously non-halting.

sections.heading: How it could halt: a second counter drains the first
html: The list behind the main run starts with a run of a ones. In a round where m leaves remainder 1 when divided by 3, that run is swallowed by the main run. In the other rounds it usually survives and grows to about 4a/3, and the main run pays: m becomes about (4m − a)/3 instead of 4m/3.

If the run survived long enough to reach four times the main run, the main run would be used up and the machine would halt: for every m below 30 that is not 1 mod 3, every a from 4m + 14 on (4m for m = 2 mod 3) halts, apart from a few values.

m mod 3what happens to the first run ahalts when
1swallowed: m′ = (4m + 3a + 8)/3never
0grows to about 4a/3, m′ = (4m − a)/3 (or swallowed)a ≥ 4m + 14
2the samea ≥ 4m

A new run starts with 2 to 17 ones, while m is in the millions after 40 rounds and keeps growing. It would have to survive hundreds of thousands of rounds in a row, each a coin flip. That is why the machine almost certainly never halts, and also why no simple pattern-based proof (a regular invariant) can exist: such a proof cannot compare the sizes of two counters, and it would have to show that the second counter stays small.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.508). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.045).
After 109 steps the tape spans 44,865 cells (32,966 left of the start, 80 right), with a density of 1s of 0.797.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

family: 4/3 Bell with a draining second counter (lottery)
summary: A 4/3 map on a run of 1s whose tail list holds a second counter that drains the main one: it halts exactly if that counter reaches four times the main run, which needs an astronomically long streak of m mod 3 ≠ 1; probviously non-halting, and no regular invariant can prove it.
